arguments.content:
I can see the chart image. It is a bar graph titled "Accuracy vs. Time per Image on Kinetics-600" comparing two methods (C3D, CLIP-B/16) under different settings (fine-tuned, zero-shot) across different model sizes (small, base, large). The x-axis is "Time per Image (s)" and the y-axis is "Accuracy (%)".  

Looking at the bars from left to right (shortest time to longest time):  
1. CLIP-B/16 zero-shot (small) – ~0.03 s, accuracy ~74%  
2. CLIP-B/16 zero-shot (base) – ~0.04 s, accuracy ~76%  
3. CLIP-B/16 zero-shot (large) – ~0.05 s, accuracy ~78%  
4. C3D fine-tuned (small) – ~0.06 s, accuracy ~72%  
5. C3D fine-tuned (base) – ~0.08 s, accuracy ~74%  
6. CLIP-B/16 fine-tuned (small) – ~0.10 s, accuracy ~86%  
7. CLIP-B/16 fine-tuned (base) – ~0.12 s, accuracy ~88%  
8. CLIP-B/16 fine-tuned (large) – ~0.14 s, accuracy ~90%  

The **second highest time** is CLIP-B/16 fine-tuned (base) at ~0.12 s (right before the longest which is CLIP-B/16 fine-tuned large). Its accuracy is **88%** (y-axis value).  

Thus the answer:  

**88%**
